title: A Data-Size Adaptive Approach to I/O of Poorly Load Balanced In Situ Data Extracts
problem: Parallel I/O performance degrades under load imbalance when output sizes and data distribution vary significantly over time, limiting throughput in in situ visualization pipelines.
motivation: Scientific simulations generate uneven data distributions across processes during in situ analysis. Standard aggregation strategies (node-based) fail to balance subfile sizes, causing I/O bottlenecks. Adaptive strategies can improve performance.
method: Data-size based aggregation strategy for ADIOS2 BP5 engine. Instead of grouping writers by compute node assignment, dynamically balances subfile sizes according to per-process data volume. Evaluated on synthetic workloads with low and severe load imbalance.
key_novelty: First data-size aware aggregation strategy for parallel I/O in ADIOS2, addressing load imbalance in in situ data extraction.
contributions: Data-size based dynamic aggregation for ADIOS2 BP5
Removes assumption that writers grouped by node assignment
Balances subfile sizes adaptively based on process-level data
Maintains or outperforms existing aggregation strategies under load imbalance
Low implementation complexity within existing ADIOS2 infrastructure
limitations: Evaluation limited to synthetic workloads; real simulation results needed. Scalability to very large systems (>10k processes) not demonstrated. Overhead of dynamic partitioning not detailed. Interaction with compression not explored.
primary_theme: Adaptive parallel I/O for unbalanced workloads
